$schema_note: Sample GuardrailPlugin policy file. Copy this into the user's project (e.g. guardrail_policy_config.json), replace the two template_id placeholders with real Model Armor templates, and retune thresholds before switching enforcement_mode to inspect_and_block. Field names mirror the Model Armor v1 REST API documented in references/model_armor_api.md.

prompt_template.purpose: Screens user prompts / model-bound requests for prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, and malicious uploads. Do not reuse this template_id for model responses.

response_template.purpose: Screens model responses for PII/sensitive-data leakage, off-brand or unsafe content, and malicious URLs. Do not reuse this template_id for user prompts.

_enforcement_mode_note: Start every new integration at inspect_only to baseline false-positive rate against real traffic; only switch to inspect_and_block after thresholds are validated (see SKILL.md Step 1 and Step 8 selftest).
_fail_mode_note: Applies only when sanitizationResult.invocationResult == 'FAILURE' (Model Armor call itself errored/all filters skipped) -- a distinct case from a content MATCH_FOUND verdict.
refusal_text: This request cannot be completed because it violates content safety policy.
_network_tools_note: Tool names (matching BaseTool.name) whose before_tool_callback args should be scanned for exfiltration risk per SKILL.md Step 5. Extend this list for any tool that makes an outbound network call.
_trusted_defaults_note: Developer-controlled baseline used by on_user_message_callback / before_agent_callback to detect and reset session-state flags that a prior model turn or tool output may have tampered with (see references/safety_plugin_patterns.md Session State Integrity).
